title: Interactive Companion for Batch+Cache Recommendations
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Design an interactive, contextual companion panel inside the Redwood Console that surfaces curated batching and caching recommendations, explains the rationale behind each suggestion, exposes safety guardrails, and lets operators preview cost/latency delta via a sandbox simulation. The companion should be lightweight (contextual strip on the right of route/model pages) and support progressive disclosure: summary recommendation -> confidence ribbon -> expandable explainers -> simulated outcome preview -> quick apply or schedule rollout. Primary goal is to help operators reduce token cost and tail latency without risking regressions to quality or SLOs.
research_notes: Usability test 2026-02-18: 6/8 operators preferred side strip for contextuality; confusion about "recommendation confidence" phrasing; strong preference for cost delta paired with example prompts
Ops interview 2026-02-05: prefer quick rollback and canary schedule options; highlight ability to pin model variants to skip risky quantized variants
acceptance_criteria: Companion panel appears on model route detail and per-route settings pages
Shows 1-3 prioritized recommendations with short rationale copy and confidence score
Interactive delta preview simulates cost and p50/p95 latency change for selected workload sample
Provides 'Apply Now' (immediate), 'Canary (10%)', and 'Schedule' rollout options wired to rollout storyboarding (frontend only)
Includes accessible tooltip explainers (A11Y), keyboard navigation, and screen-reader labels
Design spec includes tokenized microcopy for error states and fallback messaging when simulation data is missing
decisions: Use a right-side companion strip (not modal) to keep context in route settings
Confidence rendered as 3-band ribbon (Low/Medium/High) with tooltip explaining inputs: workload match, simulated improvement, safety risk
Prioritize cost delta and p95 latency over theoretical token savings in the summary view
Expose critical guardrails: preserve pinned model variants, minimum quality threshold, automatic rollback on eval regression
